page: Amazon Web Services m5.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8175M processor running at 3.1 GHz. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25% tier, which is also reflected in weak single-threaded compression and decompression speeds. However, multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations consistently rank in the middle 50% tier. The instance handles Redis SET operations at 13.15 million operations per second and static web serving at 11.92 GB/sec, demonstrating stable throughput for multi-threaded workloads.

Given its balanced resource distribution and average multi-core efficiency, the m5.4xlarge is qualitatively cost-effective for standard enterprise applications that do not require high single-thread performance or local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, multi-threaded software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and basic text processing. It can also handle light machine learning tasks, such as text generation with smaller models, though prompt processing on larger models is constrained by its CPU-only architecture.
